title: Charging & Starting System
summary: Compact charging and starting hub for battery, alternator, starter, belt, voltage, no-start, and parasitic-draw workflows.
intro: Use this hub when the complaint is battery light, intermittent no-start, no-crank, repeated dead battery, dim lights, or charging-voltage evidence.

common_symptoms.title: Battery Light On
common_symptoms.description: Use when the warning light, low charging voltage, belt slip, or alternator output needs sorting.

common_symptoms.title: Intermittent No Start
common_symptoms.description: Use when battery state, starter command, relay, cable, or ground faults may be intermittent.

common_symptoms.title: Battery Drain
common_symptoms.description: Use when the battery goes dead after sitting and parasitic draw needs verification.

common_symptoms.title: No Crank
common_symptoms.description: Use when the starter does not engage and circuit testing should come before parts.

related_repairs.title: Alternator Blueprint
related_repairs.description: Use after battery condition, belt drive, cable voltage drop, and charging output support alternator failure.

related_repairs.title: Battery Blueprint
related_repairs.description: Use when load testing, state of charge, age, or reserve capacity supports replacement.

related_repairs.title: Starter Blueprint
related_repairs.description: Use when starter command, voltage drop, and battery condition point to the starter.

related_repairs.title: Serpentine Belt Blueprint
related_repairs.description: Use when belt condition, tensioner travel, or squeal explains low charging output.

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Battery and Cable Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Start here for weak start, repeated dead battery, or voltage complaints.
checks: Charge and load test the battery before judging the starter or alternator
Inspect terminal fit, corrosion, grounds, and main power cable voltage drop
Confirm battery age and reserve capacity when the failure is intermittent
confidence_cues: Cable voltage drop can mimic failed parts

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Charging Output Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when the battery light, low voltage, or module reset pattern suggests charging trouble.
checks: Measure charging voltage at the battery and alternator output
Inspect serpentine belt, tensioner, pulley alignment, and charge fuse
Voltage-drop the alternator output and ground path before replacement
confidence_cues: Belt slip can mimic alternator failure

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Starter Command Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when the vehicle has a no-crank or click/no-crank complaint.
checks: Verify starter command signal and battery voltage at the starter
Check relay, neutral safety/clutch switch inputs, immobilizer clues, and grounds
Confirm the engine is not mechanically locked before starter approval

inspection_priority: Charge and load test the battery first.
Check cables, grounds, fuses, and voltage drop before replacing major parts.
Verify charging output or starter command under the actual failure condition.
confidence_cues: Intermittent faults may need repeat testing
Low voltage can create secondary codes
estimate_guidance: Recommend charging-system verification before alternator replacement.
Separate battery replacement from parasitic-draw diagnosis when the battery dies after sitting.
Include belt/tensioner inspection when charging voltage is low or belt noise is present.
